intro: This is the Stadium at Aphrodisias, from the 1st century AD, the best-preserved stadium of the ancient world. Both its ends still stand, and thirty rows of seats run the whole way round. It sits inside the city walls, tucked against their northern edge.
spot-1: Now you are looking at the track, the running floor of the stadium. It is thirty metres wide and rounded at both ends.
spot-2: Now you are looking at the seating. There are thirty rows on each side: room for thirty thousand people in all. Imagine the roar when they all rose at once.
spot-3: Now you are looking at the curved end. Both ends of this stadium are closed, and that is why it is the most complete stadium of antiquity.
spot-4: Now you are looking at the vaulted entrance. The crowd came in through vaulted passages like this one, at track level.
uncertainty: Finally, what this model does not know. The overall dimensions and the row count are measured. The width of the track, the depth of each step and the placing of the entrances are derived from them. The long sides bow outwards slightly, so that every row can see the whole track, but the curve in the model is proportional rather than surveyed.
